rationale: All four of my round-3 asks classified against 6cdac6e5, each re-derived: (1) Fixture marker pinning — ADDRESSED. Bead 2 step 7's new 'Fixture-state pinning (round-3 G2)' paragraph pins AC-5(ii)/(iv)/(v)/(viii) to marker-PRESENT constructions (backward states built by post-marker means, so repair's entry reconciliation no-ops and the condition under test survives to the guard), reserves the marker-absent implement/all-open state exclusively for the legacy fixture, and classifies the legacy notice as a REPLACEMENT outside AC-5(iv)'s target — exactly the pin needed to keep those legs satisfiable. (2) Sanction count — ADDRESSED, and the classification is SPEC-FAITHFUL: the taxonomy note (plan :345) scopes the round-3 G5 'exactly one unforced backward writer' sentence to ongoing v2-semantics lifecycle moves and classifies the v2 rewrite as a one-shot representation translation. I verified this is not a semantic dodge: the legacy signature requires none-closed AND none-in_progress, so the translation can never touch a genuinely-progressed epic; it runs once per epic under the durable marker; and the sanction boundary's protective intent — preventing proliferation of writers that could regress real progress — is fully preserved. The underlying lifecycle fact (never-claimed, post-plan-approve) is unchanged by the write; only its encoding moves. (3) Reset-failure re-run semantics — ADDRESSED via the materialization-marker resume, and goal (b)'s hint-execution principle now HOLDS in every window I traced: gate refusal (marker never written — it lands only after ALL gates pass) → retry meets the same gate, AC-6 intact; crash between marker write and update-ref → marker != tip, stale-delete, tip still at reviewed SHA, normal run converges; crash after update-ref before reset (the round-3 wedge) → marker == tip == C → resume skips re-snapshot/gates/panel legitimately (C's tree IS the already-gated T from the current panel round) and continues index-refresh → sync → merge, pinned by kill fixture (viii) including interval-edit-preserved-as-dirt; a foreign post-review commit → marker != tip → stale-delete → stale-SHA trips exactly as AC-7(i) demands, so the marker cannot launder ungated content on the tip-mismatch path. The documented plain re-run now provably works in the windows the op owns, which is what my ask required. (4) Bead-2 AC parenthetical — ADDRESSED, now stating the direction-conditional disposition verbatim and excluding the replacement notice. Regression scan of the rest of the diff in this lens's territory: the Windows LockFileEx replacement deviates from the spec R3.3 parenthetical's '(O_EXCL lockfile on windows)' — I judge that parenthetical DESCRIPTIVE of internal/journal's existing implementation, not a normative syscall pin; the requirement's substance (house serialization primitive, repo-scoped advisory file lock held across the critical section, same-machine boundary) is delivered strictly better by a kernel-held lock mirroring flock, and the plan says why. The ADR-0041 refusal-guarantee precision (loose objects gc-collectable, neteffect precedent) is consistent with AC-6's tip-unchanged assertion. The chunk sweep restores frontmatter/section consistency. Nothing in the fix disturbs the standing verified core (trigger-2 discharge, (c)-only vacations, dead option-2 arms, all-16-AC bead mapping). Remaining observations are info-grade; APPROVE.

findings.title: Residual non-convergent window: crash between the artifact-sync commit and the merge
findings.detail: The sync commit advances the tip to S (child of C) while the marker still points at C and is cleared only after the merge lands; a crash in that window makes the re-run classify the marker stale (C != S), delete it, and hit the panel stale-SHA gate. This is the pre-existing HEAD-class post-gate residual the honest-scope paragraph already routes to the 127 machinery, and no AC demands more — but a bead-6 implementer could cheaply extend convergence by having the sync commit re-point the marker to S (same already-gated content class: the sync commit is pathspec-confined to the named artifact no gate measures). Recorded as a design refinement option, not an ask.

findings.title: Marker-forgery trust class, considered and left to the adversary lens
findings.detail: A same-machine actor who manually writes refs/mindspec/materialized/<id> equal to a tip they also authored would make complete resume past the panel gate. This is the same local trust class as forging panel verdict JSONs or moving refs directly — MindSpec's gates protect against mistakes within a same-machine trust model, not a repo-write adversary — and the tip-mismatch path cannot launder foreign commits. Noting it so the tally sees it was weighed under this lens; adjudicating whether it needs a fence is R6 territory.

findings.title: Spec R3.3's '(O_EXCL lockfile on windows)' parenthetical vs the LockFileEx replacement — judged faithful
findings.detail: The spec's sentence cites internal/journal's acquireFileLock as the idiom to follow and describes its current mechanisms parenthetically. The plan follows the idiom (repo-scoped advisory file lock, withReportsLock-style critical section, same-machine boundary) while replacing the Windows syscall with a mechanically atomic one whose crash semantics mirror flock — the invariant R3.3 actually pins (no stale-over-fresh overwrite, serialized same-machine writers) is delivered strictly better. No spec amendment is required; the ADR/doc text landing in bead 1 should simply not claim the journal file's O_EXCL shape verbatim.
